lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Right. The Monday status meeting. I want to talk about killing it.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Finally. Who even reads the weekly status email anymore?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Nobody. It goes out at eight and by nine it's three screens down.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: So do we cancel it outright, or replace it with something?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: If we cancel it outright, what's the worst that happens?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Somebody misses a launch date and we spend a week finding out why.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Which is the thing the meeting was meant to prevent, and doesn't.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Forty-one people are on that distribution list, by the way. I counted on Monday.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: How many are on the list again?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Forty-one. Most of them were added once and never asked to be.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: That's the part that annoys me. Why do we keep adding people to things?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Because taking someone off a list feels like a demotion.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Alright. If we replace it, replace it with what?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: A written update, Monday morning, three bullets, and nobody reads it out loud.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: And where would it live? Not another document nobody can find.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: In the channel. One post, replies in the thread, done.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: I could live with that.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Hang on. What does Loom actually charge per seat these days?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: No idea at all. I haven't looked at their pricing since last year.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Then video is a maybe, not a plan.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Agreed. Written first, and we see whether anyone misses the meeting.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Should we tell people, or just stop sending the invite?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: We tell people. Quietly cancelling things is how you lose trust.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Fair. And who's writing the first one?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: I will, this week, and you can tell me it's too long.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: I absolutely will. Is anyone going to defend the meeting?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Priya might. She likes the five minutes at the end where people complain.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: That part we keep. The complaining was the only useful bit.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Decided then. Written update on Monday, meeting gone, complaints survive.
